provenance: Corrections to the imported OpenTyria tables in messages.json, from the two sources that can actually arbitrate: our own captures of client build 38797, and the client's own message-format tables recovered from Gw.exe (see studies/msgtable/FINDINGS.md). Kept beside messages.json rather than inside it so that regenerating the imported catalog cannot silently revert a verdict the client already gave us. Applying every entry here leaves zero residual disagreement between our catalog and build 38797's tables. NOTE ON RISK: the codec reads only `fields`; `declared_unpack_size`, `variable_length` and msg_header `length` are metadata it never consults. Of these entries, only GAME_SMSG 140, 146 and 421 change a field list, and Rurik sends none of those three -- so adopting this file changed no behaviour. Its value is that the catalog stops disagreeing with the binary, so later work is not built on a wrong flag. ADDED 2026-08-10: seven GAME_CMSG entries carrying `name` and the evidence for it, from two labelled input runs (toolkit/authsrv/labelrun.py, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md). The catalog had field layouts for 194 GAME_CMSG opcodes and names for NONE of them. These change NO field list -- the layouts are copied verbatim from messages.json and already agree with the client's own tables -- so they cannot affect decoding; they record what a message MEANS, which the binary's marshalling types cannot say. In particular 0x0040's u32 typing is correct and was nearly 'fixed' to float: the values are floats, the wire type is not, and the client's own SEND table says u32. ALSO 2026-08-10, later the same day: 0x0040 MOVE_UNKNOWN_FLOATS became ROTATE_PLAYER. That one was settled by the BINARY rather than by a labelled run -- the client's own assertion text names the quantity `rotation` -- and it is worth noting why the labelled runs could not have got there. A labelled run shows you WHEN a message is sent; it cannot show you that an infinity is a sentinel constant loaded from .rdata, and it was the infinities that made an angle look impossible. The wire evidence had been sitting in the vault since 2026-08-04 saying otherwise (every finite value inside +/-pi) and nobody had counted more than twelve of them.

38.name: ATTACK

61.name: MOVE_SET_HEADING
61.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C5. Field 3 (the second vec2) is a DIRECTION, not a position: across 8 samples in a session where the character COULD NOT MOVE -- so field 1 never changed -- its magnitude held at 766.8 +/- 0.4% while its angle swept the compass. A fixed-length rotating vector is a heading. This corroborates OpenTyria's TURN_TO_DIRECTION from a property the schema itself does not state. Field 4 is a small integer 1..8 whose meaning is UNVERIFIED -- it looked like an eight-way compass across 11 consecutive samples in one window and collapsed across all 26 (value 1 spans 0.0-359.1 deg), so it is NOT the absolute heading. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl.

64.name: ROTATE_PLAYER
64.why: OBSERVED, from build 38797's own binary. Field 1 is an ANGLE IN RADIANS and field 2 is a normalised turn amount in (0,1]. Both are marshalled as u32 -- which is what the client's own SEND table says ([u32,u32], wire 10 bytes), so the typing here is CORRECT and must not be 'fixed' to float -- while their VALUES are IEEE-754 float32. THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS. (1) The client names the quantity itself: the public entry 0x008165C0 range-checks its float argument against the assert text `(rotation >= -1.0f) && (rotation <= 1.0f)` from P:\Code\Gw\Char\Cli\ChCliApi.cpp line 5562, then tail-calls the sender; that argument becomes field 2 (as its absolute value) and decides field 1's sign. There is exactly ONE site in the image that sends 0x0040 -- the 12-byte wrapper at 0x009207B0, found by enumerating all 174 callers of the channel send 0x007DCF00 and recovering the opcode immediate at each. (2) The +/-inf in field 1 is a literal SENTINEL, not a computed ratio: the sender loads +inf from .rdata 0x00948654 when rotation > 0 and -inf from 0x0094E538 when rotation < 0, and when rotation is exactly 0 sends atan2(current facing) with field 2 = 1.0. So an infinity means 'turning continuously, sign gives the direction' -- it does NOT rule out an angle, which is the inference that kept this opcode unnamed. (3) The wire agrees: of 559 samples across 55 game-channel streams, field 1 is never NaN and every one of the 163 finite values lies inside +/-pi (max 3.0190), and 16 of 162 equal atan2(dir.y,dir.x) of a nearby 0x003D direction vector to float32 round-off, 33 within 0.05 rad, against a null model whose 95th percentile is 5. WHICH SIGN IS A LEFT TURN IS UNVERIFIED (121/189 and 106/169 -- real but weak); no left/right claim is made here. CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN EARLIER TEXT: 'field 2 is exactly 1.0 in all 12 observed samples' was true of those twelve and false as a generalisation -- it is 1.0 in 433 of 559, with 105 at 0.425 and a tail down to 0.10133, which CORROBORATES studies/divergence/FINDINGS.md R3 (411/536 and 105 before the 2026-08-10 runs existed) rather than refuting it. The floor is the client's own send gate: it refuses to send below 0.1, and the observed minimum is 0.10133. CORPUS CAVEAT: 536 of the 559 are the harness clicking fixed window fractions, 22 are 2026-08-10 loopback (17 of them tape-loaded), and 1 is live -- so the FREQUENCIES describe our own driver, not a player. The name does not rest on them; it rests on the binary. UPSTREAM ldufr/Headquarter numbers ROTATE_PLAYER 0x0040 independently (GWCA has 0x003E, the known +2 drift); see PLAN.md 6.1 for its register row. Evidence: vault/captures/live/20260807T143055 conn :60935 msg 52 (field1 = 1.08214450 rad = 62.0026 deg, exactly atan2 of the (360.53,678.12) direction the three preceding 0x003D carry), and toolkit/authsrv/test_rotate.py, which re-measures the wire-side invariants every run.

70.name: USE_SKILL
70.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C1. Field 1 is the SKILL ID, not the skillbar slot, and field 3 is the target's agent id. THREE witnesses: the operator named the two skills they cast before any payload was decoded; the client's own skill and string tables resolve 153 and 105 to 'Vampiric Gaze' and 'Deathly Swarm'; and the tape's own 0x00DA SKILLBAR_UPDATE declared the bar as [153, 105, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]. Pressing slots 1 and 2 sent 153 and 105 -- a slot index would have sent 0 and 1 -- and pressing the EMPTY slot 8 sent nothing at all, so the client validates occupancy locally. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl steps `skill_1`, `skill_2`, `skill_8`.

100.name: CHAT_SEND
100.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C2 and C10. Field 2 carries the typed text VERBATIM, including the channel prefix the CLIENT adds itself: typing `rurik one` sends `!rurik one`. EMOTES GO THROUGH THIS SAME MESSAGE as literal text (`/dance`, `/sit`, `/me waves`), so they are not a separate wire message and /sit is not distinguished from /dance in shape. Field 1 is the current target's agent id for slash commands and 0 for plain chat -- 6 samples across two sessions, two maps and three target allegiances, no counterexample. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl `chat_say`/`emote_dance`, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl `emote_sit`/`emote_dance`/`chat_all`/`chat_me`.

193.name: TARGET_SELECT
193.why: OBSERVED, studies/cmsg/FINDINGS.md C3, CORROBORATED across three allegiances. Field 1 is the agent to select and 0 CLEARS the selection. Three Tab presses cycled 276 -> 273 -> 274; clearing sent 0; and it preceded every USE_SKILL, every ATTACK and every INTERACT with the matching id. Seen for a hostile, a friendly NPC and another player with no difference, so it is target-select and nothing more. Evidence: vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T151946-c1.jsonl `target_tab`/`target_clear`/`attack`, vault/captures/gamesrv/authsrv-20260810T160945-c1.jsonl `target_npc`/`target_player`.

140.why: Our table stops one field short. Binary cmds[] @VA 0x00bfff98 (file offset 0x7fef98) is [0x0000008c, 0x00000404, 0x00000404, 0x00000104]; the MsgFormatRecv entry @VA 0x00bc93a0 (file 0x7c83a0) statically holds count=4, i.e. cmds[0]+3 fields, and the next cmds[] array begins exactly 4 dwords later, so there is no room for more or fewer. Slots 1..3 are zero in the file and are written by the MSVC dynamic initializer at VA 0x00464650-0x0046466e (`a1 74 f8 bf 00 / a3 9c ff bf 00` etc.), copying the statically-present constants [0x00bff874]=0x404, [0x00bff878]=0x404, [0x00bff87c]=0x104. cmd 0x104 = type 4, count 1 = a 1-byte unsigned int (our `byte`). We are missing that trailing byte, so we frame this message as 10 bytes when the client writes 11 and every later message in the datagram shifts.

421.name: GAME_SERVER_TRANSFER
421.why: Our table stops one field short AND mismarks the message variable. Binary cmds[] @VA 0x00c01b70 (file 0x800b70) is [0x000001a5, 0x00001805, 0x00000404, 0x00000104, 0x00000204, 0x00000104, 0x00000404, 0x00000104]; MsgFormatRecv entry @VA 0x00bcb36c (file 0x7ca36c) statically holds count=8 and the next cmds[] array begins exactly 8 dwords later. Initializer at VA 0x004661d0-0x00466216 copies the statically-present constants [0x00c015a8]=0x1805, [0x00c015ac]=0x404, [0x00c01668]=0x104, [0x00c015dc]=0x204, [0x00c015e4]=0x104, [0x00c01520]=0x404, [0x00c0152c]=0x104. The final 0x104 = type 4, count 1 = a trailing `byte` we do not have: 39 bytes, not 38. No type 7/11/12 field is present, so the message is FIXED, not variable_length.NAMED 2026-08-10, and it is the FIRST name any GAME_SMSG opcode has carried -- the imported catalog has field layouts for 487 of them and names for none. This one is earned the same way the seven GAME_CMSG names were: from a witness that was not consulted to make the claim. It is the GAME-channel twin of AUTH_SMSG 0x0009 GAME_SERVER_INFO. Field 1 is a sockaddr_in for the next instance (family u16 LE, port u16 BE, IPv4 -- the mixed endianness is the client's, and reading the port the other way round is a documented past failure), and fields 2, 4 and 6 are the next instance's world_id, map_id and player_id. EVIDENCE: across the three transitions in one recorded session, every one of those four values equals what the NEXT connection then sent in its own client-to-server VERSION frame -- 12 of 12 fields, parsed straight off wire.jsonl, which the decrypted channel files do not even carry. toolkit/authsrv/tape.py's chain() re-derives that every run and REFUSES a link it cannot prove, rather than ordering hops by timestamp. THE VALUES THEMSELVES ARE NOT RECORDED HERE and must not be: world_id and player_id are live session identifiers from the owner's own account, schema/ is tracked and the vault is not. Field 5 (offset +33) was 1, 0, 1 across the three hops, correlating with destination map 146/164/146 -- possibly an is-explorable flag, UNVERIFIED at n=3 with two of the three being the same map, so it stays unnamed. The 39-byte length this entry corrects is now CORROBORATED by ArenaNet's own stream as well as by the client's tables: in all three tapes the next message begins exactly 39 bytes later.
